entities.name: Bosentan
observations: Mixed endothelin-A/endothelin-B receptor antagonist; 20 mg/kg IV every 12 hours for 3 days beginning 1 hour after induction in a rat severe pancreatitis study.
In 4% sodium taurocholate pancreatitis, 7-day survival was 62% with bosentan versus 77% with vehicle; in 5% taurocholate, survival was 20% versus 27%.
The directly relevant study did not demonstrate improved survival or reduced mortality.

entities.name: Severe experimental pancreatitis
observations: Severe acute necrotizing pancreatitis was induced in rats by intraductal infusion of 1 µL/g of 4% or 5% sodium taurocholate in the bosentan study.

entities.name: PMID:10732291
observations: Büchler et al. (1999) studied bosentan in severe bile-acid acute necrotizing pancreatitis in rats; 7-day survival was numerically lower with bosentan than vehicle in both models.
The study concluded bosentan did not improve survival or other outcomes.

entities.name: LU-135252
observations: A different endothelin receptor antagonist reduced mortality from 50% to 8% in a separate rat pancreatitis study; this result is not evidence for bosentan.

entities.name: PMID:9833805
observations: A separate 1998 rat study reported lower 48-hour mortality with LU-135252, not bosentan, in severe acute necrotizing pancreatitis.
